---
title: "Reveal.js presentations"
---

## Overview

You write a reveal.js presentation the same way you write any Quarto
document — as Markdown — and choose the slide format in the front matter:

```yaml
---
format: revealjs
---
```

From there, headings become slides and the document metadata becomes a
title slide. The rest of this page walks through the slide-authoring
features Quarto 2 supports today. Each feature is paired with a small,
self-contained example project you can render and adapt; the example
projects live under
[`examples/presentations/`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations).

::: {.callout-note}
Quarto 2's reveal.js support is still growing. This page documents only
what is implemented now; features such as slide backgrounds, code-line
highlighting, transitions, themes, and the speaker-view UI are not yet
available.
:::

## Creating slides

Slide boundaries follow heading levels. A level-2 heading (`##`) starts a
slide; a level-1 heading (`#`) starts a *section*, gathering the slides
beneath it into a vertical stack; and a horizontal rule (`---`) starts a
new slide where you have no heading to give it.

```markdown
---
title: "Habits"
author: "Jane Doe"
format: revealjs
---

## Getting up

- Turn off alarm
- Get out of bed

## Going to sleep

- Get in bed
- Count sheep
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/01-creating-slides"}
[Example: 01-creating-slides](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/01-creating-slides)
:::

Sections and rule-delimited slides follow the same heading logic:

```markdown
# Part One

## First topic

Content.

# Part Two

## Another topic

Content.

---

An untitled slide, created with a horizontal rule.
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/02-sections"}
[Example: 02-sections](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/02-sections)
:::

### The title slide

When the front matter carries a `title` — and, optionally, an `author` or
`date` — Quarto opens the deck with a generated title slide. Omit those
fields and the deck starts directly on your first content slide.

### Slide level

By default, level-2 headings make slides and level-1 headings make
sections. The `slide-level` option moves that boundary: with
`slide-level: 1`, level-1 headings become slides and there are no section
stacks.

```yaml
---
format:
  revealjs:
    slide-level: 1
---
```

## Fragments

A fragment reveals part of a slide on a later click instead of all at once.
Wrap the content in a `.fragment` div, and reveal.js holds it back until you
advance.

```markdown
## Reveal on click

::: {.fragment}
Appears on the first click.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
Then this one fades up.
:::
```

Variant classes such as `.fade-up`, `.fade-out`, `.grow`, and
`.highlight-red` change how a fragment animates in. To control the reveal
order independently of source order, set `fragment-index`:

```markdown
::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}
Shown second.
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}
Shown first.
:::
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/03-fragments"}
[Example: 03-fragments](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/03-fragments)
:::

## Incremental lists

Lists are a special case of fragments. To reveal every list in the deck one
item at a time, set `incremental` globally:

```yaml
---
format: revealjs
incremental: true
---
```

To override that choice for a single list, wrap it. A `.nonincremental` list
shows all its items at once even under the global setting, and an
`.incremental` list steps through its items even when the global setting is
off:

```markdown
::: {.nonincremental}
- All three
- appear
- together.
:::
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/04-incremental-lists"}
[Example: 04-incremental-lists](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/04-incremental-lists)
:::

## Multiple columns

To place content side by side, use a `.columns` container holding two or more
`.column` divs. Each column's `width` sets its share of the row.

```markdown
:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}
Left column.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
Right column.
:::

::::
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/05-columns"}
[Example: 05-columns](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/05-columns)
:::

## Speaker notes

A `.notes` div holds commentary for the presenter. The note does not appear
on the slide.

```markdown
## A slide with notes

Slide content the audience sees.

::: {.notes}
Speaker notes go here.
:::
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/06-speaker-notes"}
[Example: 06-speaker-notes](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/06-speaker-notes)
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Speaker notes render today as a hidden `aside`; the live speaker view that
displays them while presenting is not yet available.
:::

## Asides

An aside holds content of more peripheral interest — a caveat, a citation, a
side remark. Quarto shows it small and muted at the bottom of the slide.

```markdown
## A slide with an aside

The main point, front and center.

::: {.aside}
Some commentary of more peripheral interest.
:::
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/07-asides"}
[Example: 07-asides](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/07-asides)
:::

## Footnotes

Footnotes on a slide are gathered into an aside at the bottom of *that*
slide, rather than into a single list at the end of the deck. Each slide
numbers its own footnotes from one, and when a slide carries both an aside
and footnotes, they share a single block at the bottom.

```markdown
## Per-slide footnotes

A claim that needs a citation.^[The footnote text.]

::: {.aside}
An aside and the footnotes share the bottom of the slide.
:::
```

::: {.q2-website-example-iframe example="presentations/08-footnotes"}
[Example: 08-footnotes](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/08-footnotes)
:::

To keep footnotes at the end of the deck instead — as a final slide —
set `reference-location: document`:

```yaml
---
format:
  revealjs:
    reference-location: document
---
```
